subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 18, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - October 18, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS Community,

It's been a busy week for the AcreetionOS team, with several exciting developments across various projects. We're excited to share the latest updates with you in this newsletter.

Firstly, our community has been actively contributing to the project, with several new commits and pull requests being merged into the codebase. The recent merge of the 'repair' branch has fixed a conflict with the geocode-glib update, ensuring that our distribution remains stable and up-to-date. We're grateful for the contributions of our community members, who continue to drive the project forward.

In other news, we're pleased to announce the initial commit of acreetion-surf v2.0.0, a significant update to our web interface. This new version brings improved performance and a more user-friendly experience for our users. We're excited to see how this update will benefit our community.

We're also excited to share the results of the 2026 TAB election, which saw several members of the Linux Foundation Technical Advisory Board elected. This is a significant milestone for the Linux community, and we're proud to see our community members playing a key role in shaping the future of Linux.

In addition to these updates, our team has been working on several new projects, including the introduction of GNOME OS Preview. This new feature provides a seamless and intuitive user experience, and we're excited to see how it will be received by our users.

We're also pleased to announce the initial commit of acreetion-surf v2.0.0 in the natalie/acreetion-surf repository. This update brings several bug fixes and performance improvements, making it a significant step forward for our web interface.

Meanwhile, cobra3282000 has been working on several new commits, including the force of Wayland session as the default desktop environment and the installation of lightdm-slick-greeter to fix displaymanager job crashes. These updates will improve the overall user experience and stability of our distribution.

We're also excited to see the progress being made on several new projects, including the initial commit of acreetionos-code/ember-vulkan and the initial commit of cobra3282000/downgrade-desktop. These projects have the potential to bring significant improvements to our distribution, and we're looking forward to seeing the results.

Finally, we want to thank our community for their continued support and contributions. Your involvement is what drives the AcreetionOS project forward, and we're grateful for your enthusiasm and dedication. Keep up the great work, and we look forward to seeing what the future holds for our community.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva
Co-Lead Developer, AcreetionOS
